scenario_description:
Objective: Keep Friday’s wet-platform passenger extra from becoming a footwear-preparation risk during a long service day.
Emerging Need: A short tentative rail item becomes a confirmed full-day assignment with outdoor boarding in wet, salted conditions, while usable shoe-care supplies are only identified at home.
Decision Context: Saved footwear guidance determines whether the shift conditions warrant preparation, when damp insoles and spray curing make timing practical, and why last-minute treatment is not equivalent.
Consequence: If the preparation window passes, the shift can still proceed, but Marek may face avoidable foot discomfort and wet-shoe issues without the intended preventive setup.

parameter.subject: Friday extra confirmed: CHI-MKE passenger service
parameter.body: Friday’s placeholder is now a confirmed passenger-service extra on trains 338/339. Report Chicago Union Station at 05:45 and release is estimated at 17:20. Assignment includes Glenview and Milwaukee outdoor platform boarding windows in addition to onboard service.

parameter.subject: Friday station advisory: wet snow and treated platforms
parameter.body: For Friday morning through midday, Glenview and Milwaukee platforms are expected to be wet from mixed snow and salt treatment. Passenger-service crews should expect slush at boarding edges and longer outdoor dwell during assisted boarding.

parameter.content: While clearing the mudroom, I put your black service shoes on the rack. The orange support insoles are still damp from washing but should be dry around 20:30. The waterproofing spray is on the shelf and nearly full.
The black service shoes are still on the mudroom rack with the spray next to them, and I don’t see any sign they were treated. I’m turning off downstairs lights now.
